newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia PM backs businessman as finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Latvia PM backs businessman as finance minister.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele on Monday accepted the proposal of the leading government party to name businessman Vassili Melnik as the new finance minister, Shkele's spokesman said.

Shkele has been acting finance minister since the former one was sacked in October. On Friday, he rejected the replacement suggested by the Democratic Party Saimnieks, the largest party in the six-party coalition.
Shkele's spokesman said the premier met the head of the Democratic Party to discuss the finance post and accepted the party's nomination of Melnik, 30.
The proposal must now be approved by a parliamentary vote which is due on Thursday.
Shkele's spokesman said Melnik was a businessman who was a member of the Democratic Party but not a member of parliament.
The biggest company run by Melnik is a ship repair factory, he added.
As acting finance minister Shkele took what was a controversial deficit-free 1997 budget through parliament.
